title: Fats Waller and Bessie Smith in his repertoire
summary: He sings Fats Waller and Bessie Smith numbers and says any blues or jazz tune can be done as coon shouting.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Lee, didn't you used to listen a lot? Weren't you influenced quite a bit by the records of Bessie Smith and also Fats Waller? Did you used to hear Fats sing?

Oh yes, I have quite a bit of his records and I always liked his style of singing and I think he was a wonderful piano player. I liked his style of playing and his style of singing. I do a lot of his numbers called Why Am I Neglected and Honey Keep Your Mind On Me and Honeysuckle Rose and all those numbers that he did. I liked his style. And Bessie Smith, I do her first number that she ever recorded. I have the original music on it and I sing it. It's called Golf Coast Blues, which is a popular number today and it's one of Bessie Smith's first recordings. And I guess I'm the only singer today that sings it. And I do it in coon shouting.
Lee, isn't there another one you added in your repertoire by Bessie Smith about the sea diver?

Oh yeah, I do her number called Mr. Deep Sea Diver, which is a blues tune with parodies to it and breaks. You can take most any song and do it in coon shouting. Just say we'll just use the blues. We'll just say like Memphis blues or anything. Well you take it and you sing about eight bars and you put a break in it or any blues and break it up like that. And you can do it in coon shouting or any blues. No worries. You can take any jazz tune. Just like in Way Down Yonor New Orleans and that part, stop, give your lady fair a little smile. Stop, da da da da. Well, it's a real coon shouting type of a number. If you've noticed, so many of the singers that sing that actually don't sing it like it's written.
